title: Lesson 41 · Do you call that a hat?
titleZh: 第41课 你把那个叫帽子吗？

examples.en: Do you call that a hat?
We call him Tom.
My wife was wearing a hat.
He took off his hat.
You needn't be so rude about it.
It is rude to point at people.
She looked at herself in the mirror.
He looked at his face in the mirror.
examples.zh: 他在镜子里看自己的脸。

examples.en: I sat down on a modern chair.
examples.zh: 我坐在一把新式椅子上。

examples.en: They live in a modern house.
examples.zh: 他们住在一幢现代住宅里。

examples.en: The modern chairs have holes in them.
examples.zh: 这种新式椅子上有窟窿。

examples.en: There is a hole in my sock.
'We mustn't buy things we don't need,' I remarked.
examples.zh: “我们不应该买我们不需要的东西。”我说。

examples.en: He remarked that the weather was fine.
I need not remind you of that terrible tie.
examples.zh: 我不必提醒你那条糟糕的领带。

examples.en: Please remind me to call him.
He bought a terrible tie yesterday.
examples.zh: 他昨天买了一条糟糕的领带。

examples.en: The weather was terrible.
A man can never have too many ties.
examples.zh: 男人有多少领带也不会嫌多。

examples.en: He wore a blue tie.
I find the tie beautiful.
What a beautiful garden!
The hat looked like a lighthouse!
examples.zh: 那顶帽子看起来像一座灯塔！

examples.en: The lighthouse stands on the coast.
My wife was wearing a hat.
She wears glasses.
We mustn't buy things we don't need.
examples.zh: 我们不应该买我们不需要的东西。

examples.en: You needn't have said that.
We mustn't buy things we don't need.
examples.zh: 我们不应该买我们不需要的东西。

examples.en: He bought a tie yesterday.
My wife was still in front of the mirror.
The car stopped in front of the house.

sentences.en: I sat down on one of those modern chairs with holes in it and waited.
sentences.zh: 我坐在一把带窟窿的新式椅子上等待着。

sentences.en: We had been in the hat shop for half an hour.
sentences.zh: 我们在帽店里已经呆了半个小时。

sentences.en: My wife was still in front of the mirror.
Ten minutes later we walked out of the shop together.
sentences.zh: 十分钟后，我们一起走出了商店。

sentences.en: My wife was wearing a hat that looked like a lighthouse!
sentences.zh: 我妻子戴着一顶像灯塔一样的帽子！

article.en: 'Do you call that a hat?' I said to my wife.
article.zh: “你把那个叫帽子吗？”我对妻子说。

article.en: 'You needn't be so rude about it,' my wife answered as she looked at herself in the mirror.
article.zh: “你说话不必这样刻薄，”我妻子边照着镜子边回答说。

article.en: I sat down on one of those modern chairs with holes in it and waited.
article.zh: 我坐在一把带窟窿的新式椅子上等待着。

article.en: We had been in the hat shop for half an hour.
article.zh: 我们在帽店里已经呆了半个小时。

article.en: My wife was still in front of the mirror.
'We mustn't buy things we don't need,' I remarked suddenly. 'You needn't have said that,' my wife answered.
article.zh: “我们不应该买我们不需要的东西，”我突然说。“你没必要这么说，”我妻子回答说。

article.en: 'A man can never have too many ties,' I said.
article.zh: “男人有多少领带也不会嫌多，”我说。

article.en: Ten minutes later we walked out of the shop together.
article.zh: 十分钟后，我们一起走出了商店。

article.en: My wife was wearing a hat that looked like a lighthouse!
article.zh: 我妻子戴着一顶像灯塔一样的帽子！
